turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Every autumn I throw out my geraniums and buy new ones in spring. Feels wasteful.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It is a bit. You can keep them over winter quite easily if you've got a cool, frost free spot, like a porch or a spare room.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's an unheated porch. Gets cold but never freezes.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's ideal. Dig them up before the first frost, cut them back by about half, and pot them up snugly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do they need watering all winter?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hardly at all. Just a splash once a month so the roots don't completely dry out. They'll look sad, and that's fine.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Bring them somewhere brighter, water more, and they'll push out new shoots. You can even take cuttings and double your plants for free.
